description: The GreenBook of the CSIR supports government in South Africa in adapting settlements to climate change with an online repository of downscaled baseline and future municipal climate risk data, insights and adaptation information for settlement planning. It has a national overview of interactive web apps on trends and projected changes for coastal flooding, floods, wildfires, drought, settlement vulnerability, urban growth, climate change, the economy, agriculture, forestry and fisheries, surface water and groundwater, with technical research reports; a Municipal Risk Profile Tool giving each local municipality and its settlements risk profiles to 2050 with vulnerabilities, population projections, exposure to climate hazards and impacts on key municipal resources; an Adaptation Actions Tool; MetroView high-resolution baseline and 2050 risk profiles for selected metropolitan cities; training; and planning support. A download section offers data for risk and vulnerability mapping, such as population distribution, informality hotspots, socio-economic vulnerability and water security. Access is free online; the site states all rights reserved and gives no open licence. Caveats: the tools load by script and the projections are scenario-based. Coverage is South Africa. It supports hazard exposure, resilience and capacity planning for municipal infrastructure and services; related records are the European Climate Risk Assessment viewers and the Mexico Atlas Nacional de Riesgos.
